text:
maria: quick thread — did a long-ctx sweep on mixtral-7b (32k) comparing linear / NTK / YARN RoPE. NTK run shows a clear perplexity drift starting ~8k tokens, not present in linear. attaching quick profiler and kv stats.

maria: command used:
```
./run_inference --model mixtral-7b --rope ntk --ctx 32768 --batching policy=aggressive,max_batch=64 --profile=simple --save /s3/ropexp/1937654321/
```

maria: profiler excerpt (top 10 hotspots):
```
kernel_select    41.2%   (ntk path activated at step ~8000)
attention_kv     27.9%   (kv copy + eviction spikes)
serial_io        9.8%
softmax          6.1%
kv_cache_lookup  5.4%   (miss rate rising)
other            9.6%
```

ken: :eyes: do you have kv hit/miss numbers? could be cache fragmentation w/ aggressive batching.

maria: kv metrics from the same run (aggregated):
- kv_hits: "182k"
- kv_misses: "34.5k"
- kv_evictions: "12.1k"
- avg_kv_segment_size: "6.8MB"
- observed_miss_rate: "15.9%" at t>8k

maria: for linear run at same traffic: kv_miss_rate ~4.2%, perplexity stable. so miss rate correlates with drift.

anya: did the runtime switch kernels mid-run? iirc we route to the NTK-optimized kernel only when headkv dim matches expected dims. maybe detection flipped after longer prefixes?

sam: checked kernel routing logs:
- 00:00:00 route->linear_optimized (warmup)
- 00:12:43 route->ntk_optimized (fallback)  <-- at ~7.9k tokens
- 00:12:58 route->headkv-sharded (since batch mix changed)

sam: so there is a routing handoff around the 8k mark which aligns with profiler. that handoff also toggles batching heuristic to larger groups.

liam: could larger batch groups cause KV index collisions/evictions because of prefix alignment? we've seen eviction storms when batch sizes spike and we compress kv segments.

maria: yes looks like: batching policy became "aggressive" due to throughput target, which increased max_batch from 16->64 after detecting sustained latency headroom. that reduced CPU overhead but increased concurrent KV writes. evictions spiked.

maria: short log slice showing eviction spikes:
```
[12:12:40] kv_write id=0x7f21a len=6.7MB concurrent=12
[12:12:41] kv_evict id=0x3c4f evicted=1.2MB reason=segment_full
[12:12:42] kv_evict id=0x4b9a evicted=2.8MB reason=fragmentation
```

ken: so hypothesis: NTK RoPE increases effective kv index entropy for long prefixes -> combined with aggressive batching causes higher eviction -> missing prefixes -> model sees shifted context -> perplexity drift.

anya: actionable: 1) force linear kernel routing for longctx NTK runs to confirm, 2) add kv backpressure when eviction rate > threshold, 3) instrument prefix-alignment stats.

maria: tried 1) and 2) locally: forcing linear routing keeps perplexity stable, miss_rate drops to 5.1%. enabling kv backpressure (max_concurrent_writes=8) reduces evictions by ~70% and mostly mitigates drift.

maria: quick perf diff (ntk, aggressive vs ntk+backpressure):
- perplexity @ 12k tokens: 23.8 -> 20.4
- tail token latency p95: 210ms -> 230ms (small cost)
- kv_miss_rate: 15.9% -> 5.0%

sam: small latency cost seems worth it. can we make backpressure adaptive so Dedicated customers don't see perf hit unless eviction is actually occurring?

liam: yes adaptive backpressure doable: monitor evictions/sec and scale max_concurrent_writes down when > X, otherwise anneal up. need safety cap to avoid oscillation.

maria: also interesting: on QWEN-style heads we've seen less entropy and fewer evictions under same batching, so this seems model-specific (heads/kv dim interaction). recommend per-model safe defaults.

anya: filing a follow-up: we'll add per-model rope-safe profiles: default batching caps + kernel routing hint. also add an eval to check perplexity drift for every RoPE variant on longctx.

maria: logs and full profiler: https://s3.internal.redwood/ropexp/1937654321/ (private)

infra-bot: Deploy preview created for branch ropexp/kv-backpressure-1937654321 — preview id: pr-4821 — runs on staging.

ken: next steps:
- (maria) push adaptive backpressure config prototype to pr-4821 (ETA today)
- (sam) add kernel routing guard to prefer linear when eviction_rate rising (ETA tomorrow)
- (anya) add CI eval that runs 8k->32k prefix sweep w/ perplexity log (ETA 2 days)

maria: I'll attach the minimal repro script to the PR and a small synthetic workload. thanks all. :thumbsup:

liam: :+1: keep an eye on dedicated customers with large reserved pools — they might want a knob to opt into aggressive batching despite risks.

maria: noted — will add a config flag for "throughput_priority" that overrides per-model caps (default false).

ken: great thread. saving logs and moving to follow-up ticket.

maria: filing ticket: INF-7629 "RoPE NTK longctx perplexity drift -> kv eviction interaction" with repro + PR link.
